meta: A man in red flees a flood of Bavarian People's Party ballots in Hermann Keimel's 1919 election poster.
about: A man in red runs from a flood of blue and white slips of paper marked Bayerische Volkspartei. The text says the election storm is sweeping the land and sets Bavarian blue and white against Russian red. Hermann Keimel made the poster for the Bavarian People's Party in 1919.

meta: General Akashi Gidayu writes his death poem before ritual suicide in Tsukioka Yoshitoshi's Summer-like moon, about 1880.
about: General Akashi Gidayu, in a white outfit, sits on the floor with a short sword in his right hand and papers in front of him that hold his death poem, which is also written at the upper right. A tiger is painted on the screen at his right. He is preparing to commit ritual suicide after failing to win in battle. Tsukioka Yoshitoshi made the print around 1880.

meta: A huddled group of refugees on Adolf Franz Theodor Münzer's 1919 poster warning Upper Silesians about joining Poland.
about: A huddled group of poor refugees fills the poster. Its text says this is how Polish emigrants look, and how you will look too if Silesia becomes part of Poland. It urges Upper Silesians to stay with the new Germany. Adolf Franz Theodor Münzer made the poster in 1919.

meta: A tree of life with the German eagle and the arms of Breslau, Oppeln and Liegnitz on a 1920 Silesian poster by Adolf Franz Theodor Münzer.
about: A tree of life stands with the German imperial eagle at its base and the coats of arms of three Silesian cities. They are Breslau and Oppeln, with Liegnitz at the third place. The text says Germany is the common mother earth of Upper, Middle and Lower Silesia, and it urges Upper Silesians to protect the unity of Silesia by forming patriotic associations. Adolf Franz Theodor Münzer made it in 1920.

meta: Mount Fuji seen through a wreath on a torii while bathers wash at a cistern, in Katsushika Hokusai's print of about 1836.
about: A priest stands next to a torii with a large wreath hung through it, and Mount Fuji shows in the distance through the wreath. At the left two men and a woman bathe at a cistern fed by water pouring from an opening in a tree. Katsushika Hokusai made the print around 1836.

meta: The young Oshichi, burned at the stake in 1683 for arson done out of love, in Utagawa Kuniteru's print of 1867.
about: This print shows the young maiden Oshichi, who tried to set a fire out of love and was burned at the stake in 1683. She became a figure in plays with different story lines. A small vignette above her head shows a famous place in Edo called Ai no Uchi. Utagawa Kuniteru made the print in 1867.

meta: A sword-shaped F monogram on a 1918 poster for the permanent art exhibition of the Field-Grey Artists' Association.
about: The poster shows the monogram of the Feldgrauen Künstler-Bund, a large letter F in the shape of a sword with a K and a B on either side. The text announces the permanent art exhibition of the Armed Forces Art Association and gives the place and the opening and closing times. It is an anonymous German poster of 1918.

meta: A bird's-eye view of Nihonbashi bridge with boats, shops and Mount Fuji beyond, in Utagawa Hiroshige's 1855 print.
about: The print gives a bird's-eye view of the Japan Bridge at the Nihonbashi station on the Tōkaidō Road. Boats lie on the river, and shops fill the foreground. Large buildings stand across the water, with another bridge and a temple in the near distance and Mount Fuji behind. Utagawa Hiroshige made it in 1855.

meta: Hiroshige's title page and contents for his Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, printed in 1858 over a swirling river.
about: This is the title page and table of contents for a catalog of prints from Hiroshige's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. An illustrated fan with a view of Mount Fuji and separate sheets of text lie over a background of a swirling river with flowers on its banks. Utagawa Hiroshige made the print in 1858.

meta: A Landsknecht drummer calls volunteers to join the Freischar Loeschebrand in Helmuth Stockmann's 1919 poster.
about: A Landsknecht soldier beats a drum. The text invites officers and enlisted soldiers who know all weapons to join the Freischar Loeschebrand of the Guard Cavalry Rifle Division, and it lists where to register and what benefits are offered. Helmuth Stockmann made the poster in 1919.

meta: Eggplants, a falcon and Mount Fuji from a ferry in Kitagawa Utamaro's First dream print of 1798.
about: A ferry carries a crowd of women and men and a child. One man poles the boat, and a porter sits at the back with baskets of eggplants. A man holds a falcon on his left forearm, and he and the other man may be a hunting party being ferried across the river. Mount Fuji rises in the background. Kitagawa Utamaro made the print in 1798.
dimensions: 37.2 x 23.3 cm (left panel), 37.1 x 23 cm (center panel), 37.3 x 22.9 cm

meta: The Minamoto surprise attack at Kurikara Valley in Katsukawa Shuntei's print of about 1810.
about: The print shows the chaos of a surprise night attack by the Minamoto clan on the Taira clan at the Kurikara Pass. The Minamoto used deceit to seem more numerous and drove oxen with torches tied to their horns into the Taira on the narrow pass. They attacked on several fronts and routed the larger Taira force. Katsukawa Shuntei made the print around 1810.
dimensions: 37.1 x 25.4 cm (left panel), 37 x 25 cm (center panel), 37.4 x 25.6 cm

meta: A man and a woman with long cloths by a stream on the way to Tamagawa, Torii Kiyonaga's print of 1785.
about: A man squats next to a stream with a long piece of cloth in his hands, which he may be washing, and a woman stands beside him with another long cloth. They may be servants of the more elegantly dressed woman at the right, who holds a fan. Torii Kiyonaga made the print in 1785.

meta: A porter slips and the passenger tumbles from a sedan chair under a full moon in Utagawa Hirokage's Emonzaka print of 1861.
about: A full moon shines over two porters carrying a sedan chair. The porter at the rear has slipped, and the passenger tumbles out of the chair onto the ground. Another man in geta stands nearby. Utagawa Hirokage made the print in 1861, and it shows Emonzaka at Shin-Yoshiwara.

meta: An actor as the holy man Nakasaina Sonja sitting on a frog with a fleeing dragon, in Utagawa Kuniyoshi's print of 1847.
about: An actor plays Nakasaina Sonja, a Buddhist holy man, sitting on the head of a large frog and holding an incense bowl in his right hand. A small dragon flees to the left. The print is possibly the center sheet of a triptych. Utagawa Kuniyoshi made it in 1847.

meta: The first scene of the story of the 47 rōnin, a confrontation between two officials, in Katsukawa Shunshō's 1785 print.
about: This print shows a confrontation between a court official and a lesser official, whose wife stands nearby, after an offense by the court official. It sets the stage for later acts, in which the lesser official commits ritual suicide and the 47 rōnin take revenge on the court official for their master's death. Katsukawa Shunshō made the print in 1785.

meta: A courtesan walks in the snow with two attendants under parasols in Suzuki Harunobu's print Snow, 1767.
about: A courtesan walks in the snow with two young female attendants and a male servant, who carries a large parasol. The man seems to be barefoot, and the women wear geta. Suzuki Harunobu made the print, titled Snow, in 1767.

meta: The kabuki actor Ichikawa Danzō I with a sword over his shoulder in Katsukawa Shunshō's print of 1776.
about: The kabuki actor Ichikawa Danzō I stands full-length, turned slightly left, with a sword over his right shoulder. He may be shown in the role of a samurai or of Shoki the demon queller. Katsukawa Shunshō made the print in 1776.

meta: A woman reads by a tea cabinet under a print of Daikoku shaving Fukurokuju's head, in Utagawa Kunisada's print of 1818.
about: A woman sits reading in a chair at a cabinet that holds tea utensils. On the wall behind her hangs a print of two of the seven lucky gods, Daikokuten shaving the head of Fukurokuju. Utagawa Kunisada made the print in 1818.

meta: Women wash clothes at a river while a crab holds a cloth and a child runs to the water, in Utagawa Kunisada's print of 1818.
about: Four women wash clothes at the edge of a river. One has pulled out a piece of cloth that a crab has caught hold of, and a young child dashes toward the water to see it. Utagawa Kunisada made the print in 1818.

meta: Mount Fuji across Edo Bay from Mount Kanō in Kazusa province, from a series of Thirty-six Views of Fuji, 1858.
about: This view shows Mount Fuji across Edo Bay from Rokusozan in Kazusa. In the foreground are a large evergreen tree, cherry blossoms, a torii, people and a horse. Citing Basil Stewart's guide to Japanese prints, the Library of Congress notes that it is no. 35 in the Thirty-six Views of Fuji and attributed to Hiroshige II, although the catalog credits Utagawa Hiroshige and dates it 1858.

meta: The Takino River at Ōji with a waterfall, a torii and a bridge to the cherry blossoms in Utagawa Hiroshige's 1856 print.
about: The print gives a bird's-eye view of the Takino River near the Ōji station. A steep cliff and a waterfall stand beside a walkway along the river, with a torii at the entrance to a shrine and a wooden bridge leading to an area for viewing cherry blossoms. Buildings fill the background. Utagawa Hiroshige made it in 1856.

meta: The Nakanocho boulevard at night near the Shin-Yoshiwara gate, in Utagawa Toyoharu's perspective print of 1775.
about: Many people fill Nakanocho Boulevard at night near the gate to the Shin-Yoshiwara pleasure district of Tokyo, possibly during the lantern festival. Teahouses and shops line the street. Utagawa Toyoharu made this perspective print of famous places of Japan in 1775.

meta: A woman offers a lit pipe to her lover while a man peeks from under a table, Suzuki Harunobu's print of about 1770.
about: A woman hands a lighted pipe to her lover, who reclines on a bed nearby. From an adjoining room a man, probably her husband, peeks from beneath a small table that holds part of a bird, perhaps a rooster. This is page 13 of a work by Suzuki Harunobu, made around 1770.

meta: A man clutches a long cloth held by a woman with a crane screen behind her, in Suzuki Harunobu and Ippitsusai's print of 1769.
about: A man sits on the floor clutching a long piece of cloth that the woman standing beside him holds. Her hand is on a hairpin, perhaps as she gets ready to take it out. A screen painting behind her shows a crane in flight. The print is by Suzuki Harunobu and Ippitsusai, made in 1769.

meta: Two figures that may be the lovers of the poem Loving two people equally in Suzuki Harunobu's print Jakuren Hōshi.
about: Two figures may be the two lovers from the poem Loving two people equally, based on the legend of Unai Otome. One lies on the floor reading, perhaps poetry, in a kimono decorated with origami cranes. The other stands smoking a pipe. Suzuki Harunobu made the print, titled Jakuren Hōshi, around 1760.

meta: Porters, travelers and ships at Takanawa on the Edo waterfront in Utagawa Hiroshige's print of 1837.
about: Porters carry sedan chairs, and travelers walk and ride along the waterfront at Takanawa. Ships come into port and lie at anchor in the background, and a public house stands on the left. Utagawa Hiroshige made this view of the famous places of Edo in 1837.
